Data Cleaning

Our research question is “Is there a correlation between Air Quality Health Index and income inequality in Canadian metropolitan areas?”

We’ve collected our Air Quality Health Index (AQHI) data. We now need to identify the Census Metro Areas (CMAs) associated with each Station ID.

First, let’s change our AQHI data to refer to a city rather than a station code!

library(tidyverse) #importing libraries, not all used yet
library(gtools)
library(modelsummary)
library(ggeffects)
library(data.table)
library(sf)
library(jsonlite)
library(data.table)
library(tmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(terra)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
main_dir <- "C:/Users/zaneb/Documents/Vault/UBC/24W/Term 2/ECON 326/FinalProject" #equivalent to getwd(), saved for ease

regions <- c("atl", "ont", "pnr", "pyr") #the four areas of data collection in AQHI files

d_AQHI <- lapply(setNames(regions, regions), function(region) { #lapply applies a function to a list
  dir_path <- file.path(main_dir, "Data/AQHI", region) #folder of data
  files <- list.files(path = dir_path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) #list of files in the folder
  rbindlist(lapply(files, fread), use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE) #reading all of the folders, then binding them together under separate lists in d_AQHI
})

naps <- st_read(file.path(main_dir, "Data/aqhi_station.geojson")) #read the geojson guide to the different research locations
Reading layer `aqhi_station' from data source 
  `C:\Users\zaneb\Documents\Vault\UBC\24W\Term 2\ECON 326\FinalProject\Data\aqhi_station.geojson' 
  using driver `GeoJSON'
Simple feature collection with 135 features and 5 fields
Geometry type: POINT
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: -135.0808 ymin: 42.28306 xmax: -52.72528 ymax: 68.3609
Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
valid_cgndb <- unlist(lapply(regions, function(region){
  setdiff(names(d_AQHI[[region]]), c("Date", "Hour (UTC)")) #generate a list of cgndb values in d_AQHI
}))

We need to adjust that data to correspond with different CMAs.

CMA <- st_read(file.path(main_dir, "Data/Spatial/CMA_shape.shp")) #import CMA
Reading layer `CMA_shape' from data source 
  `C:\Users\zaneb\Documents\Vault\UBC\24W\Term 2\ECON 326\FinalProject\Data\Spatial\CMA_shape.shp' 
  using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
Simple feature collection with 156 features and 8 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
Dimension:     XY
Bounding box:  xmin: 3856867 ymin: 687427.7 xmax: 8996148 ymax: 3518467
Projected CRS: NAD83 / Statistics Canada Lambert
PR <- st_read(file.path(main_dir, "Data/Spatial/PR_shape.shp")) #import PR
Reading layer `PR_shape' from data source 
  `C:\Users\zaneb\Documents\Vault\UBC\24W\Term 2\ECON 326\FinalProject\Data\Spatial\PR_shape.shp' 
  using driver `ESRI Shapefile'
Simple feature collection with 13 features and 8 fields
Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON

Projected CRS: NAD83 / Statistics Canada Lambert
PR <- st_simplify(PR, dTolerance = 10000) #simplify PR

CMA <- CMA |> filter(PRUID != "24") #filter out QC

naps <- st_transform(naps, 3347) #CRS correction
naps_CMA <- naps |> filter(lengths(st_intersects(naps, CMA)) > 0) #create a naps dataframe that includes only sites within a CMA
naps_CMA <- st_join(naps_CMA, CMA["CMANAME"], join = st_intersects) #add CMA value

naps_df <- as.data.table(naps_CMA)[, .(cgndb, CMANAME, name, longitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[,1], latitude = st_coordinates(geometry)[,2])] #prep for merge, grab name & longitude and latitude values

naps_df <- naps_df[naps_df$cgndb %in% valid_cgndb] #remove irrelevant stations

naps_df[, name := lapply(name, function(x) fromJSON(x)$en)] #adjust names to english

cgndb_key <- setNames(naps_df$name, naps_df$cgndb) #create a key of place names and cgndb values
#for(region in regions){
 # loc_names <- valid_cgndb[valid_cgndb %in% names(d_AQHI[[region]])] #create a list of names from the region
  #loc_key <- as.character(cgndb_key[loc_names]) #add the key to the list, make it chr (avoiding bug)
  #setnames(d_AQHI[[region]], loc_names, loc_key) #set new names for d_AQHI!
#}
placenames <- unlist(lapply(regions, function(region){
  setdiff(names(d_AQHI[[region]]), c("Date", "Hour (UTC)")) #making a list of cgndb now in d_AQHI
}))

Let’s map this data.

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = PR, fill = "white", color = "black") + #PR shapes
  geom_sf(data = CMA, aes(fill = "Census Metropolitan Areas"), color = "black") + #CMA shapes
  geom_sf(data = naps_CMA, aes(color = "AQHI Measuring Stations"), size = 1.2) + #naps points
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Regions",
                    values = c("Census Metropolitan Areas" = "lightblue")) +  
  scale_color_manual(name = "Locations",
                     values = c("AQHI Measuring Stations" = "red")) + 
  theme_minimal(base_family = "serif") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + #center title
  labs(title = "Map of Canadian Metropolitan Areas and AQHI Measuring Stations",
       caption = "Data source: StatCan") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(3690800, 9012300), ylim = c(687400, 5242000)) #set bounds to make sure map isn't too small

Now let’s import our census data.

d_Census <- fread(file.path(main_dir, "Data/Census/CMA_Data.csv")) #import census data

We now need to merge all of our data together into one clear dataframe.

CMA_naps <- CMA |> filter(lengths(st_intersects(CMA, naps)) > 0) #create a CMA dataframe that includes only sites with a naps

CMA_nonaps <- CMA |> filter(lengths(st_intersects(CMA, naps)) == 0) #create a CMA with sites that don't have naps
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = PR, fill = NA, color = "black") + #PR shapes
  geom_sf(data = CMA_nonaps, aes(fill = "No AQHI Measurements"), color = "black") + #CMA w/o naps
  geom_sf(data = CMA_naps, aes(fill = "Has AQHI Measurements"), color = "black") + #CMA w/ naps
  scale_fill_manual(name = "CMA Category",
                    values = c("No AQHI Measurements" = "lightblue", 
                               "Has AQHI Measurements" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "serif") + #theme, font
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + #center title
  labs(title = "Map of Canadian Metropolitan Areas with AQHI Readings", 
       caption = "Data source: StatCan") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(3690800, 9012300), ylim = c(687400, 5242000)) #scale
naps_CMA <- st_join(naps_CMA, CMA_naps["CMAUID"], join = st_intersects)#add CMAID values to naps

d_CMA <- as.data.table(naps_CMA)[, .(cgndb, CMAUID, CMANAME)] #short df of cdngb values with CMA locations & ID

aqhi_cgndb <- unlist(lapply(regions, function(region){
  setdiff(names(d_AQHI[[region]]), c("Date", "Hour (UTC)")) #making a list of placenames now in d_AQHI
}))
d_AQHI <- rbindlist(d_AQHI, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE, idcol = "region") #break apart regional grouping
d_AQHI_l <- melt(d_AQHI, id.vars = c("region", "Date", "Hour (UTC)"), variable.name = "Station", value.name = "AQHI") #shift from wide to long
d <- d_AQHI_l |>
  inner_join(d_CMA, by = c("Station" = "cgndb")) #add CMA data: stations will be labelled by CMA
d <- d |>
  group_by(CMAUID, CMANAME, Date) |>
  summarise(mean_AQHI = mean(AQHI, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") #regroup by average daily AQHI for a CMA at a given day
d <- d |>
  group_by(CMAUID, CMANAME) |> #group by CMA
  summarise(
    total_days = n(), #total days with data
    high_AQHI_days = sum(mean_AQHI > 3, na.rm = TRUE), #number of days with high AQHI
    percent_high_AQHI = (high_AQHI_days/total_days)*100, #% of days with high AQHI
    average_AQHI = sum(mean_AQHI, na.rm = TRUE)/total_days #average of daily AQHI averages
  )
d_Census <- d_Census |>
  rename(CMAUID=`Census Metro Area ID`) #change for merge

d_Census <- d_Census |>
  mutate(CMAUID = str_pad(as.character(CMAUID), width = 3, side = "left", pad = "0")) #fix formatting
d <- d |>
  left_join(d_Census, by = "CMAUID") #combine the census and AQHI data!
d <- d |>
  left_join(CMA_naps, by = "CMAUID") |> #add the geographic data!
  select(-CMANAME.y) |> 
  rename(CMANAME = CMANAME.x) #removing doubled CMANAME column
d <- st_as_sf(d) #make d recognized as spatial again
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = PR, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = percent_high_AQHI), color = "black", size = 0.2) +  #color by AQHI percentage
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "% High AQHI Days", option = "magma") + #color scale
  theme_minimal(base_family = "serif") + 
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + #center title and subtitle
  labs(title = "Percentage of Days with AQHI > 3 by Census Metropolitan Area", 
       subtitle = "Higher values indicate more frequent poor air quality.", caption = "Data source: StatCan") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(3690800, 9012300), ylim = c(687400, 5242000))

Now we can work with the data!
